precepts.text: So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man. Knit together as one man, one mind. Only the word of God can knit us together as one man.
precepts.point: The acknowledgment of the mystery of God, and of the Father, and of Christ: that goes back to the chapter before.
precepts.why:
Paul prays “That their hearts might be comforted, being knit together in love”. That is how all of us ought to be: our hearts and our minds knit together. Judges shows what that looks like: “So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man.” Knit together as one man, one mind.

In this truth we have to learn to work together. All nations do it. Chinese work together with Chinese, East Indians with East Indians, Arabs with Arabs, white folks with white folks. It's only dumb blacks and Latinos that cannot get it together, mainly black people, always with an issue, always with a problem. You can get mad if you want; you know it's true.

That is why we don't have a community. Look at the Chinese community: they have Chinese hospitals, Chinese supermarkets, Chinese banks in Chinatown. In the black community we have to go to the white communities for hospitals and grocery stores, which we don't own, and there ain't no black banks around here. So when we say we have a community, we are lying to ourselves and lying to the people. It's just BS.

Israel once gathered as one man. Only the word of God can knit us together as one man again, and that is the knitting together in love that Colossians is speaking of.

precepts.text: Saul answered, am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? Benjamin was the smallest because of the judgment poured out in this war.
precepts.point: That judgment is why Saul, in the days of the first king, calls himself a Benjamite of the smallest of the tribes of Israel; this war is what minimized the tribe. There have been mighty and righteous Benjamites since, Paul chief among them, but it is written, and we learn the history as it is written.
precepts.why:
Jump ahead to the days of the first king and hear how a Benjamite speaks of his own tribe. When Samuel comes to him, Saul answers, “Am not I a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel? and my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? wherefore then speakest thou so to me?”

Benjamin was the smallest of the tribes of Israel because of the judgment poured out in this war. Only “six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon, and abode in the rock Rimmon four months”; that remnant is all that kept the tribe from being utterly destroyed. Everything else, “the men of every city, as the beast, and all that came to hand”, was smitten “with the edge of the sword”, and the cities were set on fire.

Benjamin was judged big time. The Most High pushed the reset button on the tribe for the sodomite and rape activity that came out of Gibeah, and chapter 21 shows the drastic measures that had to be taken so Benjamin could continue producing as a tribe. That is the war that minimized the tribe, and that is why Saul calls himself a Benjamite of the smallest of the tribes.

There have been mighty and righteous Benjamites since, Paul chief among them. But it is written, and we learn the history as it is written.

precepts.point: The spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the captains, who said, "Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse: peace be unto thee, for thy God helpeth thee." David received them and made them captains.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 12: The Tribes Gather to David

precepts.why:
The tribes of Israel sent through all Benjamin asking, “What wickedness is this that is done among you?” and told them to deliver up “the men, the children of Belial, which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death, and put away evil from Israel.” “But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren the children of Israel”. Instead they “gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah, to go out to battle against the children of Israel.”

Benjamin stood with its own against all Israel. Benjamin tended to stick with Benjamin, and that is the tribal loyalty David feared. So when “there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the hold unto David”, he was leery because of the beef between him and Saul. He went out to meet them and said, “If ye be come peaceably unto me to help me, mine heart shall be knit unto you: but if ye be come to betray me to mine enemies, seeing there is no wrong in mine hands, the God of our fathers look thereon, and rebuke it.”

Then the spirit came upon Amasai, chief of the captains: “Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse”. So “David received them, and made them captains of the band.”

points: All the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was gathered together as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, unto the LORD in Mizpeh: four hundred thousand footmen that drew sword.

Israel got ready for war behind one woman, one victim. There is no hatred of women in this truth; wicked women are rebuked, which is itself love, and here a crime against one sister moved the whole nation to arms.

The children of Benjamin heard that Israel was gone up to Mizpeh. The Levite, the husband of the woman that was slain, testified: I came into Gibeah that belongeth to Benjamin, and the men of Gibeah rose against me and beset the house round about upon me by night, and thought to have slain me; and my concubine have they forced, that she is dead. Forced is the Bible's word for rape.

He said they have committed lewdness and folly in Israel. Nowhere in the Bible can rape be called lawful; it is lewdness and folly, and whether the victim lives or dies the matter is counted as murder. Be very mindful of sick, perverted camps that teach otherwise.
All the people arose as one man, saying, we will not any of us go to his tent, neither will we any of us turn into his house; none of us are going home until this is answered.

They set an order for war, ten men of an hundred throughout all the tribes to fetch victual for the people, and all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, knit together as one man. Even wicked and without a king, Israel had some morals left; gang rape was intolerable.

The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, what wickedness is this that is done among you? Now deliver us the men, the children of Belial which are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and put away evil from Israel; everything those men had going on was worthy of death.

But the children of Benjamin would not hearken to the voice of their brethren; instead they gathered themselves together out of the cities unto Gibeah to go out to battle against the children of Israel, riding for their own no matter the crime.

Benjamin numbered twenty and six thousand men that drew sword out of the cities, beside the inhabitants of Gibeah, seven hundred chosen men. Among all this people were seven hundred chosen men lefthanded, every one able to sling stones at an hair breadth and not miss: slinging with the velocity of a firearm and dead accurate. Benjamin was about that action.
The men of Israel beside Benjamin were four hundred thousand men of war that drew sword. Four hundred thousand against twenty and six thousand: you would think a landslide victory.

The children of Israel arose, went up to the house of God, and asked counsel of God: which of us shall go up first to the battle against the children of Benjamin? And the LORD said, Judah shall go up first.

Israel encamped against Gibeah and put themselves in array, and the children of Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground of the Israelites that day twenty and two thousand men. Benjamin opened the battle by giving Judah the business.

The men of Israel encouraged themselves; we cannot go out like that to the men of Gibeah. They set their battle again in array in the same place, went up and wept before the LORD until even, and asked, shall I go up again to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother? And the LORD said, go up against him.

The second day Benjamin came forth out of Gibeah and destroyed down to the ground eighteen thousand more, all men that drew the sword. Fresh legs came in against them and Benjamin still had the endurance and stamina to whip them.

Then all the children of Israel and all the people went up unto the house of God, wept, sat there before the LORD, fasted that day until even, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD. This time the whole nation humbled itself.

The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days, and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it. They asked, shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease? And the LORD said, go up; for to morrow I will deliver them into thine hand: a direct promise of victory on the morrow.
Now Israel set liers in wait round about Gibeah. No more going head up against lefthanded slingers you cannot beat straight on; now there was a strategy, an ambush.

Part of Israel put themselves in array as at other times, and Benjamin was drawn away from the city, beginning to smite and kill about thirty men and saying, they are smitten down before us as at the first. Little did they know they were falling into the plan; Israel fled on purpose and drew them from the city onto the highways.

The liers in wait came forth out of their places, even out of the meadows of Gibeah, ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and the LORD smote Benjamin before Israel: the children of Israel destroyed of the Benjamites that day twenty and five thousand and an hundred men. The victory belonged to the Most High, as he had promised.

There was an appointed sign between the men of Israel and the liers in wait, that they should make a great flame with smoke rise up out of the city. That was the purpose of drawing the Benjamites out: while Benjamin smote about thirty men and thought they were winning as in the first battles, the liers in wait hasted, rushed upon Gibeah, smote all the city with the edge of the sword, and set the sign.

When the flame began to arise out of the city with a pillar of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them, and behold, the flame of the city ascended up to heaven; and the men of Benjamin were amazed, for they saw that evil was come upon them. In that moment they knew it was over.

They turned their backs before the men of Israel unto the way of the wilderness, toward the rock of Rimmon, but the battle overtook them: eighteen thousand men of valour fell, five thousand were gleaned in the highways, and two thousand slain at Gidom, twenty and five thousand in all, including all those mighty lefthanded men of valour.

Six hundred men turned and fled to the wilderness unto the rock Rimmon and abode there four months; only that remnant kept the tribe from being utterly destroyed. The men of Israel turned again upon the children of Benjamin and smote them with the edge of the sword, men of every city, and beast, and all that came to hand, and set on fire all the cities they came to.

Benjamin was judged big time; the Most High pushed the reset button on the tribe for the sodomite and rape activity that came out of Gibeah. Chapter 21 shows the drastic measures that had to be taken so Benjamin could continue producing as a tribe.
